title: Characteristic zero at generic points of log strata
statement: For a locally Noetherian fs log scheme $(X,M)$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] and $r\in\mathbf N$, its constant-rank locus $S_r$ consists of the ordinary points $x$ for which every geometric point over $x$ has characteristic group completion of rational rank $r$. The characteristic group and its rank are those of the given log structure, not those of a Zariski replacement. Its log strata are the connected components of the $S_r$, in their subspace topology. Say that its log strata have characteristic-zero generic points when, for every $r$ and every $x\in S_r$ that is a generic point of its connected component [def-sc-generic-point], the residue field $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field] has characteristic zero. Generic means that the closure of the singleton inside $S_r$ is that connected component. This definition imposes no characteristic condition away from those generic points and includes empty schemes and empty rank loci.

source.place: VIII 3.4.14 and Theorem 3.4.15, pp.113--114: stratification by rank of the characteristic group and its maximal points.
